selector.exact: is nonempty if and only if $|X|$ is odd
selector.suffix: , and it is closed in every topo

annotations.body: The 'only if' is false. Take X = {0,1} and sigma = id: Fix(sigma) = X is nonempty and |X| = 2 is even. A brute force over every widget with |X| <= 5 finds 8 such counterexamples (referee-dm-0003.check.py, trial 1). Only the 'if' direction holds.

The congruence is correct but does not give the statement. |X| = |Fix(sigma)| mod 2 says |Fix(sigma)| is odd exactly when |X| is odd: a claim about oddness, not about nonemptiness. An even number of fixed points can be nonzero, which is the counterexample above. The step 'which gives the parity statement' hides this.

Redundant given the other hypotheses. A finite Hausdorff space is discrete, and every map out of a discrete space is continuous, so this condition is always met. Verdict: implied by another hypothesis. proved-here.
Checked and necessary. Drop it and, on three points, 9 continuous involutions leave Fix(sigma) not closed (referee-dm-0003.check.py, trial 2). Verdict: load-bearing.

selector.exact: the diagonal is closed when $X$ is Hausdorff
selector.suffix: ; the same argument in the algeb

annotations.body: Sharpening: the argument proves more work than the conclusion needs. X is finite and Hausdorff, hence discrete, so every subset is closed; the diagonal is not needed. The argument is correct, only heavier than necessary.
